_readme: Everything identical for every Comeet customer. A company record under profiles/companies/ names "platform": "comeet" and adds only what differs: slug, name, careers_url, api.endpoint (which carries both the uid and the per-company token) and health. Merged company-over-platform by profiles.resolve_profile, then validated as one document.

israel_filter._note: VERIFIED live 2026-08-13. post_fetch is the correct and only method here, per SKILL Step 5: the API has no location parameter at all - every query parameter tried (page, limit, offset, skip, and location-shaped ones) was ignored and returned the identical full board. So there is nothing to filter with before fetching; the single call returns every posting worldwide and relevance is decided after the fetch. `structure: none` records that Comeet's API exposes no location filter, not that its hosted careers page lacks one. checked_fields gained location.city and location.country on 2026-08-19: location.name alone is a company-authored label and was silently dropping 47 Israeli postings - see api._note.

api._country_code_note: Set 2026-08-20, and it is an OPT-IN that no platform gets by default. It lets a NON-Israeli location.country reject a posting - the other half of a field that until now could only ever add. Earned by auditing the field across all 202 live Comeet boards on that date: location.country took 60 distinct values over ~3,200 postings and every non-empty one was a bare two-letter code ('IL' 1520, 'US' 967, 'GB' 105, 'IN' 102, ...). It is a dropdown, not prose. 143 postings carry NO code (106 empty string, 37 null), which is exactly why an absent code still means nothing and rejects nobody - is_foreign_country_code answers False for empty, missing and unparseable alike. Measured blast radius: 10 postings dropped at 4 companies, every one a US role the text filter had no way to see - faye 4 ('Remote - East Coast', a coast rather than a state), linx_security 3 ('U.S. Remote', which _normalize turns into 'u s remote' so the `us` marker cannot match), atera_networks 2 and sentra 1 (a bare 'Remote' on a US req in a board of Tel Aviv ones). Zero Israeli postings lost, no company dropped to zero, no health gate tripped. Six further at-risk postings are deliberately kept because their text names an Israel-inclusive region the single-country picker contradicts - see relevance.ISRAEL_INCLUSIVE_REGIONS. Removing this key restores the pre-2026-08-20 behaviour exactly, with no code change.
api._note: The stable id is `uid` (e.g. '71.E67'), NOT `id` - Comeet has no top-level `id` field, and falling back to the link would produce a different key for the same posting the moment the slug in that URL changed. Verified 238 unique uids across the largest board in the set. `url_comeet_hosted_page` is an absolute www.comeet.com link; `url_active_page` also exists and points at the company's own branded careers page, but it is not always present and sometimes carries a tracking query - the hosted page is the one that is always there. `extra_params` adds &details=true to the one listing call. That single parameter is what carries every posting's description in the listing itself - see detail_fetch below for why it replaced a per-posting page fetch. *** location_city and location_country were added 2026-08-19 and are load-bearing. *** `location.name` is FREE TEXT the company types itself, and an audit of all 108 boards found it holding a website ('www.final.co.il'), a page name ('careers'), an office nickname ('GK8 by Galaxy'), a street address, a region ('EMEA') and a misspelt city ('Herzeliya') - on postings whose location.country was 'IL' every time. Reading it alone dropped 47 Israel-relevant postings at 9 companies, four of which had consequently never delivered a single alert. location.city and location.country are picker values, not free text, which is what makes them trustworthy; fetch_comeet reads all three. See api.fetch_comeet.

detail_fetch._note: VERIFIED live 2026-08-18 against all 105 Comeet boards in this project: 105/105 returned a populated `details` array. *** THIS REPLACES A BLOCK THAT WAS COSTLY, NOT WRONG. *** The previous block used method='embedded_json' to scrape POSITION_DATA out of each posting's hosted page, and it worked - but at one extra HTTP GET and ~1.06s per NEW posting, against the run-wide MAX_DETAIL_FETCHES_PER_RUN cap of 40. That cap is the single thing that stops this project scaling past a few hundred companies: one company reworking its board spends the whole run's allowance, and every posting past it stays 'undetermined', which fails open and is delivered untriaged. What was missed earlier is that the listing endpoint DOES serve the description - it just needs &details=true, which the previous note explicitly (and incorrectly) ruled out. Cost measured on fetcherr: the board response grows 57 KB -> 244 KB, once per company per run, and the per-posting requests drop to ZERO and become uncapped. Shape is the same {name, value} section array the embedded_json path was reaching, so inline_section_heading/content are unchanged and the 'Requirements' heading still becomes an <h3> via render_sections - which is what makes its bullets count as mandatory in experience.classify_block.

health._note: Both fields are overridden per company by the importer from that company's live verified count, because they are per-company facts and a platform-level default for them is meaningless. The defaults here are the SAFE direction: expected_min_jobs 0 disables the absolute floor (leaving the relative-collapse gate, which needs no per-profile number), and zero_is_plausible false means a company dropping to zero is treated as a fault rather than shrugged off.

notes: Endpoint template: https://www.comeet.co/careers-api/2.0/company/{uid}/positions?token={token}. One call, a flat JSON array, the entire board - no pagination of any kind (verified against vastdata/43.001, the largest board in the set at 238 postings: page, limit, offset and skip were all ignored and returned the same 238). THE TOKEN IS NOT THE UID - it is a separate per-company public value published in the JSON blob embedded in the company's Comeet-hosted board page (https://www.comeet.co/jobs/{slug}/{uid}), next to its company_uid. Using the uid as the token returns HTTP 400 'Account uid or token are not valid' for every company. The token is resolved ONCE at import time and baked into api.endpoint, never re-resolved at runtime: the board page is ~750 KB against a few KB for the API call, so resolving 104 tokens per run would add ~78 MB to every scheduled execution for data that effectively never changes. If a company's token is ever rotated its fetch returns HTTP 400, which surfaces as an ordinary fetch failure and reaches the maintenance alert after two consecutive runs. Full evidence: _onboarding/verify_report.md.
